walkthroughs.body_html:
A bond is polar if electronegativity difference > 0.4. A molecule is polar only if dipoles do not cancel by symmetry.

CO2 has polar C=O bonds but is linear so dipoles cancel: non-polar overall. H2O is bent so dipoles add: polar.

Order of strength: H-bond > permanent dipole-dipole > London (vdW). London forces grow with electron count (larger Mr).

Boiling points: HF > HCl due to H-bonding. Branched alkanes have lower bp than straight chains (less contact area).

Requires H attached to N, O or F, plus a lone pair on another N/O/F. The H is partially positive, attracted to the lone pair.

Explains the anomalously high bp of H2O, ice being less dense than water (open lattice), and DNA base pairing.
